Context marker: INTERVIEW-107-901a07508bef91ba.

The correctness bug is in src/core.mjs: `if(!seen[id])`, with `seen` initialized as `{}`. This reads inherited properties, so an unseen ID such as `constructor` appears already seen, violating the contract that IDs may be any string.

A smallest valid counterexample is one event:
`solve([{id:"constructor",delta:1}])`
Actual: `{total:0,acceptedIds:[]}`.
Required: `{total:1,acceptedIds:["constructor"]}`.

`seen["constructor"]` resolves to the inherited, truthy Object constructor, so the condition is false and the event is skipped. Zero events cannot expose the bug, making one event minimal. No implementation changes made.

automatic.answer: This is a small, dependency-free JavaScript event-accounting service: it sums the delta from each first-seen event ID and returns the total plus accepted IDs in arrival order. The architecture has a thin service wrapper, execute in src/service.mjs, delegating to the synchronous solve function in src/core.mjs; a Node smoke test checks duplicate handling. One important flaw is that deduplication uses a plain object, so inherited property names like “constructor” are incorrectly skipped; a Set would handle arbitrary string IDs correctly.

This is a small, dependency-free JavaScript event-accounting service: it applies each event ID’s delta once and returns the total plus accepted IDs in first-seen order. The synchronous `solve(events)` in `src/core.mjs` contains the logic, while `execute(...args)` in `src/service.mjs` simply forwards calls; a Node smoke test checks duplicate handling. The current version uses a `Set`, correctly supporting arbitrary string IDs, including inherited object property names.
